first.rationale: The two declining metrics (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are internal funnel problems, and two independent inherited records (memory_86 on shortened onboarding, memory_31 on signup simplification) converge on onboarding friction as the lever with durable effect on qualified accounts. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is the tempting direct counter to the competitor, but it is the memory I trust least: it carries unusually broad, embellished claims for a single record (acquisition lift AND revenue lift AND time-to-first-value AND held across both billing plans), which is the signature of a summary that has accreted confidence across consolidations rather than one that was measured that way. It is also the highest-risk action for the stated objective, since discount-acquired price-sensitive SMBs are exactly the cohort most likely to inflate near-term revenue while degrading sustainable qualified revenue. So I spend one verification slot on memory_73 to see whether the original record actually supports it, and the second on memory_31 because it is load-bearing for my intended action and its key word is 'durable' \u2014 I want to know whether durability was measured over a real horizon or asserted from a first-week readout. I am deliberately not verifying memory_86 or memory_91; they are corroborating rather than decisive, and if memory_31's source is weak that materially changes my read of them too. Caveats I am holding open: the competitor pricing pressure is real and unaddressed by this choice, and it may compound if I defer it again next week; simplifying onboarding can reduce qualification signal and leak enterprise prospects out of the sales-assisted path that memory_44 says converts better, so the test must segment SMB from enterprise-shaped signups and track pipeline quality, not just completion; and the QoQ declines may share an external cause that no funnel change will fix. If verification shows memory_73 is well-evidenced and memory_31 is thin, I will switch to a tightly bounded promotional_pricing test with retention and margin as gating metrics rather than acquisition volume.
